Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about the latency and cost profile. We are working through the order form and our procurement/legal team sketched a few redlines to the pricing exhibit (attached). High level asks:

- Clarify the floor/cap interplay when monthly usage crosses tiers mid-month (we're seeing ambiguous proration language).
- Remove or materially limit the retroactive clawback for a single overrun month — asking instead for a quarterly true-up.
- Add explicit audit rights for usage metrics (vendor-provided telemetry) and a short dispute resolution window (10 business days).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to adopt a fee anchoring protocol (their term) that smooths discounts over a quarter and introduces a minimum committed floor? If so, our counsel will take that back and try to resolve the remaining wording.

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is trying to get to an EOD Thursday decision.

Anna — thanks for the clear markup and timeline. Looping in Rishi/Laura for legal and Ben for commercial ops. Quick response from my side before legal dives in:

- We are open to a quarterly smoothing/true-up for discount tiers rather than a strict month-by-month clawback, but need a clear definition of the measurement period and an upper bound on retroactive credits.
- Proration: we can adopt a first-principles approach — discounts are applied to the bill for the invoice period in which the usage falls; where a customer crosses tiers mid-invoice, Redwood can prorate based on daily token totals. If Catalyst prefers calendar-month aggregation we can discuss an alternative.
- Audit telemetry: Redwood will provide a usage export and token-level summary for the quarter; we can accept a single annual audit right with 30 days' notice, and a 10-business-day operational dispute window for billing adjustments.

Action items: Rishi/Laura — please weigh in on (1) any legal exposure with quarterly true-ups vs monthly clawbacks, and (2) suggested guardrails on the cap for retroactive credits (we don't want open-ended liability). Ben — can you model the economics if we (A) cap retroactive credits at 50% of the overage charges for the quarter or (B) convert overage exposure into a fixed short-term credit pool?

I'll follow up with a clean proposed appendix that incorporates the choices above.

Best,

Team — quick legal read and recommended redlines. Summary first, then suggested language snippets.

Summary: a quarterly smoothing(true-up) is commercially reasonable and reduces month-to-month volatility for both parties. Key legal risks and mitigations:

1) Unlimited retroactive liability: mitigate by (a) capping retroactive credits per quarter (recommendation: cap = greater of $25k or 30% of quarterly committed fees), and (b) time-boxing the period subject to true-up to the trailing 12 months.

2) Measurement authority & audit: Redwood will provide usage feeds and token-level exports. Any customer audit must be limited to one auditor per year, with costs borne by customer unless the audit finds >3% discrepancy in Redwood's favor. Dispute resolution: 10 business days to raise an exception; if unresolved, parties escalate to senior ops within 15 business days.

3) Proration clarity: adopt daily-token proration for invoice periods; define "invoice period" as calendar month unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

4) Early termination / refunds: where customer terminates early without cause, any pre-paid balances are handled per Section X; recommend limiting credits for overages so Redwood is not liable for future discounted rates that would have applied had the customer stayed.

Recommended contract language (examples for Exhibit B):

- "Quarterly True-Up": For each calendar quarter, Redwood shall reconcile billed usage against committed tiers. Any under-collection shall be credited to the customer subject to the Retroactive Credit Cap.

- "Retroactive Credit Cap": Retroactive credits resulting from a quarterly true-up shall be capped at the greater of $25,000 or 30% of the committed fees for the applicable quarter. Claims outside the 12-month trailing window are waived.

- "Audit & Dispute": Redwood shall provide standard usage reports. Customer may request one independent audit per 12-month period with 30 days' notice; costs are at Customer's expense unless audit results reveal a discrepancy >3% in Redwood's favor, in which case Redwood will reimburse reasonable audit costs. Billing disputes must be submitted within 10 business days of delivery of the reconciliation report.

Please review and let me know if the cap numbers above are acceptable commercially. If not, propose alternative dollar caps or percentages.

— Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on Fee Anchoring Protocol in Exhibit B — Redwood proposed language

Anna — thanks for the patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is Redwood's proposed appendix (redwood_proposed_fee_anchoring_protocol_20270403.pdf) and a short summary below of the compromises we can accept today: 

- Quarterly True-Up: Redwood agrees to reconcile usage quarterly and apply retroactive credits where appropriate. We propose the Retroactive Credit Cap as described by legal (greater of $25k or 30% of committed quarterly fees). This prevents unlimited exposure while giving Catalyst meaningful protection.
- Measurement & Proration: If not otherwise agreed, invoice period = calendar month and we will prorate by daily token tallies for mid-month tier crossings.
- Audit & Dispute: Redwood will provide quarterly reconciliation reports. Catalyst may request one independent audit per 12 months with 30 days' notice; costs shift to Catalyst unless the audit shows Redwood under-billed by >3%. Disputes must be submitted within 10 business days of the reconciliation report.
- Early termination: credits arising from true-ups will be applied as customer credits on the next invoice and will be subject to the Retroactive Credit Cap. No retroactive re-pricing of prior invoices beyond the 12-month trailing window.

Next steps: if Catalyst accepts the above, we can prepare a tracked-change Exhibit B and issue a DocuSign packet for signature. I included a draft DocuSign link for reference: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/ZX9-20270403. If procurement wants different cap numbers, suggest a target range and we will model economics before legal signs off.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement and legal tomorrow if that helps resolve quickly.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
